title: Washington Admin Code: WAC 296-46B
briefing: The administrative companion to RCW 19.28 — WAC 296-46B. Ten questions on Washington's electrical rules. 70% to pass.

questions.prompt: When will the 2026 NEC replace the currently adopted 2023 NEC edition in Washington State?
choices: January 1, 2026
July 1, 2026
December 31, 2026
January 1, 2027
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-010: The 2026 NEC will replace the 2023 edition effective December 31, 2026, as adopted by reference under WAC 296-46B-010.

questions.prompt: Which of the following NEC Annexes are specifically included in the adoption of the 2023 NEC?
choices: Annexes A, B, and C only
Annexes D, E, and F only
All Annexes A through H
No Annexes are adopted — only the main body of the NEC
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-010: Washington adopts the 2023 NEC (NFPA 70-2023) by reference, including Annexes A, B, and C specifically.

questions.prompt: What is the Washington-specific definition of 'Administrator'?
choices: The L&I official who issues electrical permits in a given county
The person who qualifies a contractor's license by passing the required exam
A journey level electrician who supervises apprentices on a job site
The foreman designated to oversee a project with more than ten workers
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-100: Washington's definitions supplement NEC Article 100, and 'Administrator' is defined as the person who qualifies a contractor's license by passing the required examination.

questions.prompt: WAC 296-46B adds GFCI requirements beyond the NEC for which type of location?
choices: Commercial kitchens in restaurants
Dwelling units
Industrial machinery rooms
Outdoor agricultural facilities
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-210-008(A): Washington adds extra GFCI requirements for dwelling units beyond those required by the NEC. WAC 296-46B-210-008(B) covers other-than-dwelling units separately.

questions.prompt: How must branch circuits serving common areas in a multi-family building be arranged?
choices: Common area circuits may share the same panel as individual dwelling unit circuits
Common area branch circuits must be on separate circuits from individual dwelling units
Common areas must be served by a dedicated transformer
Common area loads may be split evenly across any dwelling unit panels
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-210-025: Washington requires that common area branch circuits be on separate circuits from individual dwelling units in multi-family buildings.

questions.prompt: Ground fault protection testing is required for feeders over 150V to ground in solidly grounded wye systems at or above what ampere rating?
choices: 600 amperes
800 amperes
1000 amperes
1200 amperes
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-215-010: Ground fault protection testing is required for feeders over 150V to ground in solidly grounded wye systems rated 1,000 amperes or greater.

questions.prompt: WAC 296-46B requires what document for certain electrical projects?
choices: A load calculation stamped by a licensed engineer
Feeder diagrams submitted to L&I before permit issuance
A signed affidavit from the property owner
An arc-flash hazard analysis
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-215-005: Feeder diagrams are required for certain projects and must be submitted to L&I as part of the plan review or permit process.

questions.prompt: What is Washington's rule regarding concrete-encased grounding electrodes at new buildings on permanent concrete foundations?
choices: They are permitted but not required, consistent with NEC 250.52
They are required only if ground rods exceed 25 ohms resistance
They are MANDATORY — a Washington amendment requiring them at all new buildings on permanent concrete foundations
They are required only for buildings taller than three stories
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-052: This is a critical Washington amendment. While NEC 250.52 uses 'shall be permitted' language, WAC 296-46B-250-052 makes concrete-encased grounding electrodes MANDATORY at all new buildings on permanent concrete foundations.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum allowable resistance to earth for a single ground rod, pipe, or plate electrode before a second electrode must be added?
choices: 10 ohms
25 ohms
50 ohms
100 ohms
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-053(A)(2): Ground rods, pipes, or plate electrodes must have a resistance to earth of 25 ohms or less. If a single rod exceeds 25 ohms, a second electrode must be installed.

questions.prompt: A grounding electrode conductor subject to physical damage must be protected by which of the following?
choices: Only rigid metallic conduit (RMC) is acceptable
PVC Schedule 40, Schedule 80, or EMT
Rigid metallic conduit, IMC, rigid nonmetallic conduit, or EMT
Wireways, auxiliary gutters, or surface metal raceways
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-064: Where a grounding electrode conductor is subject to physical damage, it must be protected by rigid metallic conduit, intermediate metal conduit (IMC), rigid nonmetallic conduit, or EMT.
